 Featured Dana White UFC White House SNL star brands UFC boss Dana White ‘evil’ over fighter pay and ties to President Donald Trump
 Donagh Corby Fri 6 November 2026 10:00 Follow us on Google Discover Saturday Night Live star Sarah Sherman has called UFC CEO Dana White ‘evil’ over his deep political ties. 
 President Donald Trump has become a vital part of the whole UFC experience in recent years, appearing cageside at countless major events and welcoming White as a key ally. Their close relationship culminated in a massive fight night taking place on the White House lawn this summer.
 Where does Freedom 250 rank among the greatest UFC events ever?
 Joe Rogan labelled it the 'greatest night in combat sports history'
 Was UFC Freedom 250 the best UFC event ever? Credit: Jacquelyn Martin- Pool/Getty Images Comment Like or Comment Have your say Sign-in now for free However, President Trump’s approval ratings continue to plummet for a variety of reasons. And after a disastrous showing for Republicans in this week’s Mid-Term Elections, White’s continued backing of his friend has been called into further question.
 READ MORE: Josh Hokit responds after Dana White admitted to giving him unfavorable UFC matchups 
 Dana White slammed by SNL star Sarah Sherman and comedian Stavros Halkias
 When Dana White first made a public endorsement of President Donald Trump and spoke on his behalf at the Republican National Convention, it marked a notable shift from the UFC boss. Previously relatively apolitical, he explicitly began to embrace the American right.
 Now, according to comedian Stavros Halkias, the Trump love-in that has taken over the sport has made MMA borderline unwatchable. During an episode of his Stavvy’s World podcast uploaded this week, he and SNL star Sarah Sherman discussed the UFC boss’ uncomfortable political shift in detail.
 Sherman told Halkias how she had become a massive fan of the fight game through her brother’s interest as well as recommendations from comedian Jack Bensinger. However, she noted that she can’t bring herself to attend events due to the right wing nature of the shows these days.
 “My brother Jack and Jack Bensinger got me really addicted to UFC this summer,” she said, to which Halkias replied ‘that’s awesome’. “I feel like I could get them tickets, I could get us all tickets to go. But isn’t it a little evil? It’s just, Dana White is evil.”
 Halkias then added in quite crude terms that being very close with White in today’s climate makes you “the dumbest person alive”. Sherman agreed, repeating that any such person is “evil”.
 “You’re stupid or evil or both, probably,” Halkias continued. “If you’re still sucking Trump’s c—, you’re a moron. And I believe Dana White has been throating him pretty well recently. That has put a real dampener on my appreciation of the sport.”
 SNL’s Sarah Sherman bemoans fighter pay issues in UFC
 Sherman, a relatively avant garde artistic type, might come as something of a surprising ally to UFC fighters over their purses. However, she seems to be clued in to the struggle of the athletes, complaining about it to Halkias as they continued their talk.
 If Dana White allowed you to pick a new location for a UFC event, where would you pick?🏖️
 The UFC continues to land in new locations, but there are still some popular destinations left.
 Photo by Antonio Masiello/Getty Images Comment Like or Comment Have your say Sign-in now for free “You know that they don’t get paid?” Sherman asked, perhaps overstating the severity of the situation. “They get annihilated.” Halkias replied that the pay structure is ‘so f—ed up’ because the real earning comes in performance bonuses for most fighters.
 “The problem is, culturally, these guys won’t unionize because it’s ‘gay’,” he continued. “It’s like ‘you kill what you eat’ which is crazy.” 
 Sherman then noted that “the background of Mixed Martial Arts is working class,” and admitted that she finds watching the sport ‘the most amazing thing I’ve ever seen’. She also made it clear that she is represented by WME, who are a majority owner of the TKO Group that includes UFC.
 Halkias then noted that he and his siblings no longer go out to watch fights due to the company’s ‘MAGA’ relationship. He said that unless an event is unmissable, he will actively choose not to support them by streaming the shows.
